property_summary: When calling transfer with a non-empty tos array and valid token contract, P returns true and M returns false.
When _tos.length > 0, reference transfer returns true while mutant reverts.

After calling transfer with a legitimate token contract that has a transferFrom function, the reference contract succeeds (returns true) while the buggy contract fails because it calls approve with wrong parameters, causing a revert.
Calling transfer with a token contract that implements transferFrom (reference succeeds) vs approve (buggy version fails because approve expects different arguments).
When _tos has exactly 1 element, the reference contract does not revert (require(_tos.length > 0) passes), but the mutant reverts (require(_tos.length > 1) fails).

After calling transfer with from=alice, tos=[bob, charlie], values=[10, 20], and letting the token contract on the second transfer return false, the reference reverts the entire transaction (so the fact that c returns true is never reached) while the bug silently continues and returns true.
With a token contract that fails on the second transferFrom call, the reference reverts (transfer returns false via try/catch) while the buggy version returns true.

After calling transfer with from=alice, caddress=a token that reverts on the second transferFrom, tos=[bob, charlie], values=[10, 20], the reference reverts the whole transaction, while the bug silently continues and returns true.
